mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE increase > 0.5% MoM does not correlate with subsequent economic weakness indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in real estate sales (HOUST) signals a weakening demand in the housing market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of declining HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% MoM signals strengthening economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increase > 1% MoM does not correlate with subsequent positive economic indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% signals a loosening monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or FEDFUNDS decrease > 0.25% does not correlate with subsequent loosening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in real GDP (GDPC1) and decrease in retail sales (RSAFS) signals a shift in consumer spending patterns, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint behavior of GDPC1 and RSAFS does not correlate with subsequent shifts in consumer spending patterns.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 signals weakening labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or PAYEMS decrease > 100,000 does not correlate with subsequent weakening labor market conditions.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5% signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, especially during an economic expansion regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal during economic expansion, or FEDFUNDS increase > 0.5% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.
